thread:
Dana Ortiz: Quick heads-up: I'm proposing a pluggable strategy surface for routing decisions. main constraints: zero-single-request blocking on plugin install, safe isolation (sandboxing), and clear canary workflow for customers. high-level doc draft below.

Ravi Kumar: sandboxing? do you mean WASM or containerized JVM? both have perf/security tradeoffs.

Dana Ortiz: right. options considered: 1) WASM runtimes (fast start, strong memory limits) 2) language plugins in sidecar containers (process isolation, heavier). preference leaning WASM for hosted flow, container plugins for Private where customers need full libs.

Nina Park: if WASM, we need deterministic memory caps and CPU cgroups, plus syscall filtering. also plan for a hot-reload signal so changing tenant policy doesn't require restart.

Owen Li: lifecycle concerns: install -> validate -> warm -> activate. validation includes ABI check, schema_version, and quick sim-run on representative requests. sim-run must be bounded time (50ms).

Dana Ortiz: rollout playbook idea: stage 0: feature-flag off; stage 1: enable for internal tenants with read-only plugins; stage 2: small external canary (non-critical tenants); stage 3: wider rollout with throttled activation. canary-bot: canary cluster created: policy-plugin-canary-7

Ravi Kumar: failure handling: plugin timeout, crash, degraded perf. resolver should gracefull-fallback to core policy engine and increment a fallback_reason metric with tags (timeout/crash/invalid). we must also limit retries per-tenant to avoid thundering re-inits.

Nina Park: critical: tracing. add a span for plugin.evaluation that includes plugin_version, warm/cold flag, and decision_time. p95 should be instrumented and trigger alert if >50ms. telemetry-bot: new metric template created: plugin.eval.latency.{p50,p95,p99}

Owen Li: config for Dedicated: allow pre-warm hooks so infra can preallocate warm WASM instances on a pool dedicated to the tenant. need API for ops to request warm_count.

Dana Ortiz: security checklist: signed bundles, attestations for Private, restrict network egress from plugin, and run a quick static linter for banned APIs. Recommend HSM-backed signature verification.

Ravi Kumar: tests: fuzz the plugin edge cases. sim harness must cover: high-qps jitter, intermittent plugin crashes, and slow init storms. add mem/handle leak checks.

Nina Park: design for observability: trace tree should show fallback paths. if fallback occurs, include plugin_id and a diagnostic code in the response metadata for engineers. avoid exposing tenant plugin details to other tenants.

Owen Li: backwards compatibility: the resolver API will accept both legacy rule bundles and plugins. legacy rules remain default until plugin is marked active for tenant. transition tools: convert-legacy -> plugin tool to ease migration.

Dana Ortiz: ownership: I'll land an RFC with lifecycle diagram and staging checklist. Owen will prototype warm-hook API. Ravi will draft the security/signing plan. Nina will stub telemetry dashboards and alerts. timeline: RFC by EOW, prototype in 3w, internal canary in 8w.

Ravi Kumar: thanks, will sync with security on attestations.

Nina Park: I'll start dashboard mocks and share links here when ready.

Dana Ortiz: Great. tagging follow-ups: @Owen Li please add warm-count API sketch, @Ravi Kumar link to signing spec, @Nina Park telemetry dashboard links. will schedule a 30min followup next Tues.
